Abomasnow: They appear when the snow flowers bloom. When the petals fall, they retreat to places unknown again.
Aerodactyl: A Pokémon that roamed the skies in the dinosaur era. Its teeth are like saw blades.
Aggron: It claims an entire mountain as its own. The more wounds it has, the more it has battled, so don’t take it lightly.
Alakazam: The spoons clutched in its hands are said to have been created by its psychic powers.
Ambipom: Split into two, the tails are so adept at handling and doing things, Ambipom rarely uses its hands.
Amoonguss: It moves the caps on both arms and does a dance to lure prey. It prefers damp places.
Arcanine: The sight of it running over 6,200 miles in a single day and night has captivated many people.
Azelf: When Azelf flew, people gained the determination to do things. It was the birth of willpower.
Azumarill: Its long ears are superb sensors. It can distinguish the movements of things in water and tell what they are.
Bisharp: This pitiless Pokémon commands a group of Pawniard to hound prey into immobility. It then moves in to finish the prey off.
Blastoise: The jets of water it spouts from the rocket cannons on its shell can punch through thick steel.
Blaziken: Flames spout from its wrists, enveloping its knuckles. Its punches scorch its foes.
Blissey: The eggs it lays are filled with happiness. Eating even one bite will bring a smile to anyone.
Breloom: Its short arms stretch when it throws punches. Its technique is equal to that of pro boxers.
Bronzong: In ages past, this Pokémon was revered as a bringer of rain. It was found buried in the ground.
Celebi: It has the power to travel across time, but it is said to appear only in peaceful times.
Chandelure: The spirits burned up in its ominous flame lose their way and wander this world forever.
Chansey: A kindly Pokémon that lays highly nutritious eggs and shares them with injured Pokémon or people.
Claydol: This mysterious Pokémon started life as an ancient clay figurine made over 20,000 years ago.
Clefable: Their ears are sensitive enough to hear a pin drop from over a mile away, so they’re usually found in quiet places.
Cloyster: It fights by keeping its shell tightly shut for protection and by shooting spikes to repel foes.
Cobalion: It has a body and heart of steel. It worked with its allies to punish people when they hurt Pokémon.
Cofagrigus: Grave robbers who mistake them for real coffins and get too close end up trapped inside their bodies.
Conkeldurr: Rather than rely on force, they master moves that utilize the centrifugal force of spinning concrete.
Cresselia: On nights around the quarter moon, the aurora from its tail extends and undulates beautifully.
Crobat: Having four wings allows it to fly more quickly and quietly so it can sneak up on prey without its noticing.
Darmanitan: When one is injured in a fierce battle, it hardens into a stone-like form. Then it meditates and sharpens its mind.
Donphan: It attacks by curling up then rolling into its foe. It can blow apart a house in one hit.
Dragonite: It is said to make its home somewhere in the sea. It guides crews of shipwrecks to shore.
Drapion: It takes pride in its strength. Even though it can tear foes apart, it finishes them off with powerful poison.
Dusclops: It seeks drifting will-o’-the-wisps and sucks them into its empty body. What happens inside is a mystery.
Dusknoir: It is said to take lost spirits into its pliant body and guide them home.
Electivire: The instant it presses the tips of its tails onto an opponent, it sends over 20,000 volts of electricity into the foe.
Empoleon: If anyone were to hurt its pride, it would slash them with wings that can cleave through an ice floe.
Espeon: Its fur is so sensitive, it can feel minute shifts in the air and predict the weather...and its foes’ thoughts.
Excadrill: Forming a drill with its steel claws and head, it can bore through a steel plate, no matter how thick it is.
Exeggutor: It is called “The Walking Jungle.” If a head grows too big, it falls off and becomes an Exeggcute.
Feraligatr: It usually moves slowly, but it goes at blinding speed when it attacks and bites prey.
Ferrothorn: By swinging around its three spiky feelers and shooting spikes, it can obliterate an opponent.
Flygon: Known as “The Desert Spirit,” this Pokémon hides in the sandstorms it causes by beating its wings.
Forretress: It is encased in a steel shell. Its peering eyes are all that can be seen of its mysterious innards.
Froslass: It freezes prey by blowing its -58 degrees F breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.
Gallade: When trying to protect someone, it extends its elbows as if they were swords and fights savagely.
Garchomp: It is said that when one runs at high speed, its wings create blades of wind that can fell nearby trees.
Gastrodon: Long ago, its entire back was shielded with a sturdy shell. There are traces of it left in its cells.
Gengar: The leer that floats in darkness belongs to a Gengar delighting in casting curses on people.
Gliscor: It dances silently through the sky. When it approaches prey, it can land a critical hit in an instant.
Gyarados: Once it begins to rampage, a Gyarados will burn everything down, even in a harsh storm.
Hariyama: It loves to match power with big-bodied Pokémon. It can knock a truck flying with its arm thrusts.
Haxorus: Its tusks are incredibly destructive. They can easily slice through a thick, sturdy steel column every time.
Heatran: Its body is made of rugged steel. However, it is partially melted in spots because of its own heat.
Heracross: No matter how heavy its opponents, it flings them far away with its prized horn.
Hippowdon: It is surprisingly quick to anger. It holds its mouth agape as a display of its strength.
Hitmonlee: Its legs can stretch double. First-time foes are startled by its extensible reach.
Hitmontop: It fights while spinning like a top. The centrifugal force boosts its destructive power by 10.
Honchkrow: If one utters a deep cry, many Murkrow gather quickly. For this, it is called “Summoner of Night.”
Hydreigon: It responds to movement by attacking. This scary, three-headed Pokémon devours everything in its path!
Infernape: It uses unique fighting moves with fire on its hands and feet. It will take on any opponent.
Jellicent: Its body is mostly seawater. It’s said there’s a castle of ships Jellicent have sunk on the seafloor.
Jirachi: It is said to have the ability to grant any wish for just one week every thousand years.
Jolteon: By storing electricity in its body, it can shoot its bristlelike fur like a barrage of missiles.
Kabutops: It is thought that this Pokémon came onto land because its prey adapted to life on land.
Kangaskhan: It raises its offspring in its belly pouch. It lets the baby out to play only when it feels safe.
Keldeo: When it is resolute, its body fills with power and it becomes swifter. Its jumps are then too fast to follow.
Kingdra: It lives in caves on the seafloor and creates giant whirlpools every time it moves.
Krookodile: Very violent Pokémon, they try to clamp down on anything that moves in front of their eyes.
Kyurem: This legendary ice Pokémon waits for a hero to fill in the missing parts of its body with truth or ideals.
Kyurem-Black: This legendary ice Pokémon waits for a hero to fill in the missing parts of its body with truth or ideals.
Landorus-Therian: From the forces of lightning and wind, it creates energy to give nutrients to the soil and make the land abundant.
Lanturn: Lanturn’s light can shine up from great depths. It is nicknamed “The Deep-Sea Star.”
Latias: Its body is covered with a down that can refract light in such a way that it becomes invisible.
Latios: A highly intelligent Pokémon. By folding back its wings in flight, it can overtake jet planes.
Lucario: By reading the auras of all things, it can tell how others are feeling from over half a mile away.
Ludicolo: If it hears festive music, all its muscles fill with energy. It can’t help breaking out into a dance.
Machamp: Its four muscled arms slam foes with powerful punches and chops at blinding speed.
Magneton: The stronger electromagnetic waves from the three linked Magnemite are enough to dry out surrounding moisture.
Magnezone: Sometimes the magnetism emitted by Magnezone is too strong, making them attract each other so they cannot move.
Mamoswine: When the temperature rose at the end of the ice age, most Mamoswine disappeared.
Meloetta: The melodies sung by Meloetta have the power to make Pokémon that hear them happy or sad.
Mesprit: When Mesprit flew, people learned the joy and sadness of living. It was the birth of emotions.
Metagross: With four linked brains, it’s more intelligent than a supercomputer, and it uses calculations to analyze foes.
Mew: Because it can use all kinds of moves, many scientists believe Mew to be the ancestor of Pokémon.
Mienshao: Using the long fur on its arms like whips, it launches into combo attacks that, once started, no one can stop.
Milotic: Its lovely scales are described as rainbow colored. They change color depending on the viewing angle.
Mismagius: Its cry sounds like an incantation. It is said the cry may rarely be imbued with happiness-giving power.
Moltres: One of the legendary bird Pokémon. It is said that its appearance indicates the coming of spring.
Nidoking: One swing of its mighty tail can snap a telephone pole as if it were a matchstick.
Nidoqueen: Its entire body is armored with hard scales. It will protect the young in its burrow with its life.
Ninetales: Each of its nine tails is imbued with supernatural power, and it can live for a thousand years.
Omastar: It is thought that this Pokémon became extinct because its spiral shell grew too large.
Politoed: It gathers groups of others as their leader. Its cries make Poliwag obey.
Porygon-Z: Its programming was modified to enable work in alien dimensions. It did not work as planned.
Porygon2: It was upgraded to enable the exploration of other planets. However, it failed to measure up.
Quagsire: It has an easygoing nature. It doesn’t care if it bumps its head on boats and boulders while swimming.
Qwilfish: It shoots the poison spines on its body in all directions. Its round form makes it a poor swimmer.
Raikou: It is said to have fallen with lightning. It can fire thunderbolts from the rain clouds on its back.
Registeel: Tempered by pressure underground over tens of thousands of years, its body cannot be scratched.
Reuniclus: They use psychic power to control their arms, which are made of a special liquid. They can crush boulders psychically.
Rhyperior: It can launch a rock held in its hand like a missile by tightening then expanding muscles instantly.
Roserade: Luring prey with a sweet scent, it uses poison whips on its arms to poison, bind, and finish off the prey.
Rotom-Frost: Its electric-like body can enter some kinds of machines and take control in order to make mischief.
Rotom-Heat: Its electric-like body can enter some kinds of machines and take control in order to make mischief.
Rotom-Mow: Its electric-like body can enter some kinds of machines and take control in order to make mischief.
Rotom-Wash: Its electric-like body can enter some kinds of machines and take control in order to make mischief.
Sableye: It hides in the darkness of caves. Its diet of gems has transformed its eyes into gemstones.
Salamence: As a result of its long-held dream of flying, its cellular structure changed, and wings grew out.
Sceptile: The leaves that grow on its arms can slice down thick trees. It is without peer in jungle combat.
Scizor: It raises its pincers with eyelike markings for intimidation. It also swings them down dangerously.
Scrafty: It pulls up its shed skin to protect itself while it kicks. The bigger the crest, the more respected it is.
Scyther: The sharp scythes on its forearms become increasingly sharp by cutting through hard objects.
Seismitoad: By putting power into its bumps, it creates vibrations and increases the power of its punches.
Sharpedo: Its fangs rip through sheet iron. It swims at 75 mph and is known as “The Bully of the Sea.”
Shaymin: The flowers all over its body burst into bloom if it is lovingly hugged and senses gratitude.
Skarmory: Its heavy-looking iron body is actually thin and light, so it can fly at speeds over 180 mph.
Slowbro: Though usually dim witted, it seems to become inspired if the Shellder on its tail bites down.
Slowking: Being bitten by Shellder gave it intelligence comparable to that of award-winning scientists.
Snorlax: When its belly is full, it becomes too lethargic to even lift a finger, so it is safe to bounce on its belly.
Spiritomb: Its constant mischief and misdeeds resulted in it being bound to an Odd Keystone by a mysterious spell.
Staraptor: It never stops attacking even if it is injured. It fusses over the shape of its comb.
Starmie: Its core shines in many colors and sends radio signals into space to communicate with something.
Steelix: The iron it ingested with the soil it swallowed transformed its body and made it harder than diamonds.
Suicune: It races around the world to purify fouled water. It dashes away with the north wind.
Swampert: It can swim while towing a large ship. It bashes down foes with a swing of its thick arms.
Tangrowth: Even if one of its arms is eaten, it’s fine. The Pokémon regenerates quickly and will go right back to normal.
Tentacruel: It extends its 80 tentacles to form an encircling poisonous net that is difficult to escape.
Terrakion: Spoken of in legend, this Pokémon used its phenomenal power to destroy a castle in its effort to protect Pokémon.
Thundurus-Therian: As it flies around, it shoots lightning all over the place and causes forest fires. It is therefore disliked.
Togekiss: It shares many blessings with people who respect one another’s rights and avoid needless strife.
Tornadus: In every direction it flies, creating winds so powerful, they blow everything away.
Torterra: Some Pokémon are born on a Torterra’s back and spend their entire life there.
Toxicroak: The croaking that Toxicroak produces before a battle is for churning the poison it has stored in its poison sac.
Tyranitar: The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.
Umbreon: When exposed to the moon’s aura, the rings on its body glow faintly and it’s filled with a mysterious power.
Ursaring: In its territory, it leaves scratches on trees that bear delicious berries or fruits.
Uxie: When Uxie flew, people gained the ability to solve problems. It was the birth of knowledge.
Vaporeon: Its cell composition is similar to water molecules. As a result, it can’t be seen when it melts away into water.
Venusaur: After a rainy day, the flower on its back smells stronger. The scent attracts other Pokémon.
Victini: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being’s entire body will be overflowing with power.
Virizion: Legends say this Pokémon confounded opponents with its swift movements.
Volcarona: Thought to be an embodiment of the sun, it appeared during a bitterly cold winter and saved Pokémon from freezing.
Weavile: They communicate by clawing signs in boulders and work together to surround enemies.
Weezing: Inhaling toxic fumes from trash and mixing them inside its body lets it spread an even fouler stench.
Xatu: This odd Pokémon can see both the past and the future. It eyes the sun’s movement all day.
Yanmega: It prefers to battle by biting apart foes’ heads instantly while flying by at high speed.
Zapdos: A legendary Pokémon that is said to live in thunderclouds. It freely controls lightning bolts.
